paper_a.title: Local Rademacher Complexities (Bartlett, Bousquet, Mendelson, Annals of Statistics 2005)

paper_b.title: Poisson Statistics for the Largest Eigenvalues in Random Matrix Ensembles (Soshnikov 2005) [REGISTRY MISMATCH: pair was curated as Koltchinskii 2006 'Local Rademacher Complexities and Oracle Inequalities', but paper285's PDF/extraction is Soshnikov]

metadata.description: Registry mismatch: paper285 was supposed to be Koltchinskii 2006 (Annals of Statistics, local Rademacher complexities and oracle inequalities), which would have given an EXT/PR/AP relation to BBM 2005. The actual extracted content of paper285 is Soshnikov's 'Poisson Statistics for the Largest Eigenvalues in Random Matrix Ensembles' (heavy-tailed Wigner / band / sample-covariance random matrices, Frechet / Poisson edge limits, Tracy-Widom universality). This is a different field (random matrix theory / extreme eigenvalue statistics) from BBM (statistical learning theory / empirical-process generalization bounds). The two papers share no mathematical objects, definitions, theorems, methods, or proof techniques. Per spec, this pair must be classified NEG until paper285 is re-extracted from the correct PDF.

matches.explanation: Star-hull of a function class around $f_0$ is a construction internal to empirical-process theory (used to make local Rademacher averages sub-root); paper285 (random matrix edge statistics) has no such object.
Rademacher average $E R_n F$ is the central complexity measure of BBM; paper285 deals with random matrix eigenvalues and never invokes Rademacher complexities.
Empirical (conditional) Rademacher average $E_\sigma R_n F$ has no counterpart in paper285's random matrix setting.
Sub-root function $\psi$ is the technical regularity class enabling local Rademacher fixed-point analysis; absent from paper285.
Loss class $\ell_F$ is a learning-theory object; paper285 has no loss/risk machinery.

Empirical Gram matrix appears in BBM only for RKHS-class bounds. Although paper285 also studies empirical (random) matrices, the role and analysis are different (sample-covariance edge spectrum vs kernel-feature inner-product matrix used to bound a Rademacher average).
Bounded-variance deviation bound (Theorem 2.1 of BBM) is a Talagrand/Bousquet-style empirical-process concentration inequality; paper285 has no analogue.
Containment of an $L_2(P)$ ball inside an $L_2(P_n)$ ball (Corollary 2.2) is BBM's data-dependent localization tool; no parallel in paper285.
Sub-root continuity and unique fixed-point lemma (Lemma 3.2) is paper-original to BBM; no analogue in paper285.
Local-Rademacher error bound (Theorem 3.3) is the main result of BBM. Paper285's main results (Theorems 1-3) concern Poisson edge statistics for heavy-tailed random matrices, an unrelated phenomenon.
Star-hull-yields-sub-root lemma (Lemma 3.4) is paper-original to BBM; not in paper285.
Bound for nonnegative bounded functions (Corollary 3.5) has no counterpart in paper285.
Empirical-ball converse (Lemma 3.6) is paper-original to BBM; not in paper285.
VC-class bound (Corollary 3.7) is a BBM-specific application; paper285 has no VC theory.
Peeling-bound technical lemma (Lemma 3.8) is the BBM peeling device; absent from paper285.
Proof of Theorem 3.3 (peeling + sub-root + Lemma 3.8) has no analogue in paper285's proofs (which use Gaussian integral / Poisson functional methods).
Second part of the proof of Theorem 3.3 (alternative weighting class with sharper constants) is BBM-specific; no parallel in paper285.
Proof of Lemma 3.6 (contraction + Theorem 2.1) has no counterpart in paper285.
Empirical local-Rademacher error bound (Theorem 4.1) is the data-dependent companion of BBM Theorem 3.3; no parallel in paper285.
Empirical/expected fixed-point comparison (Theorem 4.2) is BBM-specific; not in paper285.
Fixed-point ordering lemma for sub-root functions (Lemma 4.3) is BBM-specific; absent from paper285.
Proof of Theorem 4.1 has no analogue in paper285.
Empirical local Rademacher loss bound (Corollary 5.1) is BBM-specific; no parallel in paper285.
Empirical risk minimizer near-optimality (Theorem 5.2): an ERM consistency statement; paper285 has no ERM/risk framework.
Conditions for excess-risk bounds (Bernstein-type variance assumption, $L$-Lipschitz loss) are pure learning-theory hypotheses; not in paper285.
Distribution-dependent excess-risk bound (Corollary 5.3) is BBM-specific; no parallel in paper285.
Data-dependent excess-risk bound (Theorem 5.4) — the headline ERM oracle inequality of BBM — has no counterpart in paper285.
Iterative fixed-point convergence lemma (Lemma 6.1) for sub-root functions; absent from paper285.
Iterative fixed-point procedure (algorithm) for computing $r^*$; paper285 has no algorithms (only a proof and a Gaussian-integral computation).
Classification local-Rademacher bound (Corollary 6.2) is BBM-specific; not in paper285.
Classification complexity via weighted ERM (Theorem 6.3); no analogue in paper285.

Empirical eigenvalue bound for kernel classes (Lemma 6.6): bounds an empirical Rademacher average via empirical Gram-matrix eigenvalues. Even though paper285 also studies eigenvalue statistics of empirical (sample-covariance) matrices, the goal (controlling a function-class complexity in a fixed RKHS) and the conclusion (a deterministic bound by the truncated eigenvalue tail) are unrelated to paper285's Poisson/Frechet asymptotics for top eigenvalues of heavy-tailed matrices. Listed as `none`, not `analogous`, because no concrete object/result is shared.
Excess-risk bound for kernel-class regression (Corollary 6.7) is the BBM application to RKHS; no parallel in paper285.
Comparison of expected and conditional Rademacher averages (Lemma A.4), paper-marked as origin: paper. Empirical-process tool; no counterpart in paper285.
Empirical risk minimization for excess loss (problem statement). Paper285 has no ERM problem.
Kernel-class regression on RKHS unit ball; not present in paper285.
Real symmetric aperiodic band random matrix definition; no analogue in BBM (which has no random matrix theory).
Hermitian band random matrix definition; absent from BBM.
Periodic (toroidal) band matrix definition; absent from BBM.
Heavy-tail marginal distribution condition $G(x)=h(x)/x^\alpha$, $0<\alpha<2$; not used in BBM.
Frechet normalization constant $b_n$; not in BBM.
Sparse Cauchy matrix model; not in BBM.
Theorem 1 (Soshnikov): Poisson statistics for largest eigenvalues of heavy-tailed Wigner/band matrices. Random-matrix limit theorem; no analogue in BBM.
Frechet-type limit law for the $k$-th largest eigenvalue; no analogue in BBM.
Theorem 3 (sparse Cauchy sample-covariance determinantal limit); no analogue in BBM.
Proof sketch of Theorem 3 via Gaussian integral representation and Poisson-functional matching; no counterpart in BBM (which uses peeling + sub-root + Talagrand concentration).
Counts $N_n$ of independent nonzero entries (Wigner / periodic band / aperiodic band); paper-original auxiliary equation, no parallel in BBM.
Open problem: full Poisson statistics for heavy-tailed sample-covariance matrices; not in BBM.
Open problem: phase transition between Tracy-Widom and Poisson regimes; not in BBM.
Open problem: localization for aperiodic band random matrices; not in BBM.
